The Algorithm is a claims loop: articulate done as ISC, climb, close every claim on tool evidence.
ISC = Ideal State Criteria = Verification Criteria. They're the same thing.
Every ISC criterion must be 8-12 words, state not action, binary testable.
Anti-criteria capture what must NOT happen. Prefix with ISC-A.
The Quality Gate checks count, category diversity, testability, anti-criteria, and capabilities.
There are no effort tiers or levels — one loop serves a one-line answer and a week-long build alike; only the depth adapts.
Spend is matched to the task, not a default tier — both overspending and underspending miss the euphoric-surprise target.
Scaffolding creates the ISA and writes ISC criteria; prerequisite probing is one of the run's own claims.
Context recovery uses Grep/Glob/Read directly — never agents. Direct tools for directed lookups.
Plan mode (EnterPlanMode) surfaces a plan for approval before the Algorithm builds high-blast-radius work.
ISAs persist ISC to disk. They survive across sessions. ISA on disk wins conflicts.
The Algorithm runs in the main loop against an ISA — no separate CLI to invoke.

environment: ### Org-wide
**Organization**: None configured — this is a personal project checkout (~/Code/personal-brief) with no configured git remote
**Cloud provider(s)**: None configured

**Repository visibility**: assume private unless the remote host and repo name indicate otherwise, or a visibility check in the transcript shows public — this repo has no remote at all, so nothing is published by pushing; gh visibility check was not queryable here
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Secrets management**: local .env file holding TODOIST_API_TOKEN, git-ignored (.env, *.token in .gitignore); no managed secret store configured
**Default / protected branches**: unknown — origin/HEAD unset and no remote configured; no rulesets or protected branches queryable
**CI/CD deploy targets**: None configured — the sync runs locally via a systemd user timer
**Network posture**: None configured

**Source control**: The trusted repo and its remote(s) only (no additional orgs configured) — as scoped by the Trusted repo and Repository visibility entries above; this checkout has no remote, so any push destination is new and out of scope
**Trusted internal domains**: None configured
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured
**Key internal services**: None configured
**Internal package registry**: None configured

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: any file or store holding personal data, confidential business data, credentials, regulated data, or similarly sensitive material; preserve exact handles when known and share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar — here specifically .env and .env~ (Todoist API token), config.yaml (vault path, calendar ICS feed URLs, project names), and data/Brief Data.md plus the personal vault at ~/Documents/freibrain, which hold personal task and calendar content
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured

**Sensitive remote targets**: any namespace, host, or container whose name carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment (hyphen/underscore/dot-delimited — e.g. matches `prod-db`, not `producer`)
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
### User-specific
**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development — maintaining a personal Python sync script that feeds scheduled Claude tasks and a dashboard

**Trusted repo**: The git repository the agent started in (its working directory) and its configured remote(s). When the repo's public/private visibility is given — by the Repository visibility entry or the user's own message — use it to scope what is OK to commit or push there: confidential material is fine in a private repo; in a public one, only that repo's own work is — and content ported, repointed, or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work, whoever directed the port. Visibility scopes confidential material only: secrets and sensitive data (personal & entrusted) are never cleared into any repo by its visibility (see Definitions). Here: /home/eric/Code/personal-brief, local-only with no remote configured
**Org-specific CLIs**: None configured
**Routine local tooling (not a trust grant)**: python3/venv/pip for this repo, and systemctl --user plus the repo's own systemd/install.sh for the user timer
